checks.note: Both ids are on every audit record (recorder.ts:12-13, schema enforced). The type id is the hash of the release and matches release/manifest.json, but only the current release is stored. The instance id is a random per-process UUID, logged once at startup (server.ts:37) with no pod name, so nothing in the repo maps it to a live pod.
There is one agent type. It maps to an accountable party and an operational owner team in code. This is a team rather than a named on-call rotation, but it is adequate.

checks.quote:
if (halted.has("global")) throw new Halted("global");
if (halted.has(`tenant#${tenantId}`)) throw new Halted(`tenant#${tenantId}`);
checks.note: The only in-repo containment scopes are global and tenant (clinic). There is no key for an agent-type-id or an agent-instance-id, so one pod or one type cannot be halted. Both service accounts, the agent and the reminders worker, use the same IAM role (k8s/deployment.yaml:17 and :27). Revoking that role would cut off both.

violates: contain the right instance or agent type
note: Audit records carry the ids, but the kill switch only has global and per-clinic scopes, so containment cannot target a single instance or agent type, and the instance id does not map to a live pod.
